promptPrefix: Vintage B-movie film still, Technicolor or grainy monochrome, theatrical lighting —
promptSuffix: A frame from a real 1950s–1970s genre film: theatrical, deliberately camp, rubber-suit monsters and painted backdrops. The subjects may be heroes, villains, mad scientists, creatures or aliens.
variantDirectives: Wide set frame showing the whole painted backdrop, the figures small:
Full-length theatrical pose, camp gesture carries the drama:
Dramatic close-up lit from below, faces fill the frame:
Stark high-contrast composition, one hard stage light, minimal detail:
The set and creature effects dominate the frame, the figures secondary:
Costume and monster suits take centre stage, the figures posed to show them:

translations.terror vs. desire: the pull toward what frightens you most
translations.alive vs. undead: the question of what separates the living from those who only seem to be
translations.run vs. stay: the choice the body makes before the mind does
translations.known vs. unknown: the known world at the edge of the completely unknown
translations.safety vs. dread: the feeling that safety is temporary
translations.victim vs. survivor: the difference made only in retrospect
translations.ordinary vs. monstrous: the monster wearing a familiar face
translations.love vs. survival: what you would sacrifice for whom
translations.science vs. nature: the experiment that went further than intended
translations.before vs. after: the before and the after with the storm between
translations.awake vs. nightmare: the uncertainty about which one this is
translations.alone vs. together in the dark: the company that makes darkness worse
translations.scream vs. silence: what the throat does when the mind shuts down
translations.real vs. hallucination: the unreliable evidence of your own senses
translations.past vs. haunting: the thing that followed you home
